title: Maps from a weakly contractible affine to finite constant objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $U$ be an affine object that is weakly contractible, meaning that for every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the map $F(U)\to G(U)$ is surjective. For every profinite set $S$, write $X[S]$ for the pro-etale object obtained as the inverse limit of finite disjoint unions of copies of $X$ indexed by finite quotients of $S$. The connected-component quotient $\pi_0(|U|)$, with its quotient topology, is profinite, and there is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,X[S])\cong C(\pi_0(|U|),S)$, compatible with maps in $S$ and with morphisms between such $U$.

source.place: Section 4.2, Lemma 4.2.13(1), together with the finite-quotient inverse-limit argument; exact master RefactorInstruction.tex, Section 4, proof of Lemma point-pullback formula.

proof.text: For affine U, install its IsAffine instance. The existing compactSpace_connectedComponent and t2Space_connectedComponent instances, together with Mathlib ConnectedComponents.totallyDisconnectedSpace, prove the three topological properties. Affine schemes are compact and quasi-separated, and all schemes are prespectral. This is the same component-quotient argument as the old first step, already proved in the source library.

For a ring R, send a ring map LC(S,Z) to R to the first coordinate of its spectrum map. Its inverse is the proved LocallyConstant.liftPrimeSpectrum of the integer cast map. For a locally constant function g and a prime p of R, the characteristic idempotent of the fibre through the selected point is outside p, hence becomes one in R_p. Multiplying by it proves that the localized image of g is its evaluation. Equality at every prime localization proves the first inverse law; LocallyConstant.comap_liftPrimeSpectrum proves the second. Compose this explicit equivalence with Spec.homEquiv and transport along the affine isomorphism. The construction is inside the existing specMapEquiv definition and does not depend on the removed private Basic helpers.

The pullback defining X[S] and terminality of Spec Z give (U →_X X[S]) ≃ (U → Spec LC(S,Z)): project along pullback.fst; invert by pullback.lift with the fixed structural map U → X. The pullback identities and hom_ext prove the inverse laws. Compose this equivalence with the preceding affine correspondence and the connected-components lifting equivalence to construct e. No arbitrary witness is chosen and weak contractibility is not needed.

At a representative x of a connected component, e(f)([x]) is the first coordinate of the image of x in Spec LC(S,Z) under the homeomorphism with S × Spec Z. The affine transport cancels by its inverse identities; Spec.homEquiv cancels with Spec.map. For b:S → T, write a prime as the evaluation prime at (s,p). Precomposition on locally constant functions sends its comap to the evaluation prime at (b(s),p), so the first coordinate is b(s). The pullback map has the expected first projection by pullback.lift_fst. These pointwise identities prove target naturality after quotient-surjectivity and continuous-map extensionality.

For a:V → U, represent a component of V by x. The connected-components map sends [x] to [a(x)]. Both sides of source naturality are therefore the same first coordinate of f(a(x)) after projection from X[S]. Definitional composition and extensionality prove the equality. All equivalences and inverse laws also apply to empty sources, empty targets, singleton targets and the zero ring; none uses nonemptiness or nontriviality.

proof_origin.place: The proved liftPrimeSpectrum, algebraMap_localization_liftPrimeSpectrum, comap_liftPrimeSpectrum and equality in every prime localization. The elementary characteristic-idempotent inverse argument also appears in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.CondensedFieldContinuousRealization; that module imports this item and cannot be imported back. Affine transport, the terminal-Spec-Z pullback equivalence and pointwise naturality complete the proof below unit level.
